Messages.Author: Miller Delmardigan
Messages.Body:
Card Text:

Mortal with 1 life, 1 strength, 0 bleed.

Arms dealer may take a +1 stealth action to allow you to search your library
for a weapon and move it to your hand. Discard to your hand size and shuffle
your library afterward.

When the Arms Dealer uses is capacity, is the player forced to reveal the
weapon he retrieves to all players ?

Or can he hide the weapon he retrieves, thus playing the Arms Dealer's
capacity in a trustful manner ?

How can the other players be sure that the card retrieved *is* a weapon ?

Miller Delmardigan

Sabbat Priscus

Messages.Author: Andy Brown
Messages.Body:


Whenever we play that you look for something, then you must reveal to
all
players, to ensure that it is correct, unless specified.

One exception to this is moving blood to a younger uncontrolled vampire,
but you could always call a judge to ensure this is OK.

--

> >

> > so play nice. :-)
>

> I assume this is the same for anything along these lines then.

If no card text to the contrary, true. General rule: do not assume rules or
procedures that are not printed in the rules or on a card. Since there's neither
a rule nor card text to state that the weapon fetched must be displayed for the
other players, then don't assume it.

> I.E. The Summoning, where the only person you would have to prove a card type to
> would be the judge.

Card text quote from The Summoning (inferior presence text):
"Search your library for an ally or retainer. Show it to all players and put it in
your hand..."

(Using the superior version obviates this need to resolve this issue anyway.)

It's uncertain whether "proving" the card's type was ever the reason for this rule.
If it were, one would expect that the text of Arms Dealer would have been updated
to bring it into line with some of the other cards that have functions of this type,
like The Summoning. Assuming no dishonesty issues, the one *concrete* effect of
the extra text in cards like The Summoning is that your opponents are allowed to
see exactly what card you've brought into your hand. That point seems more likely
to explain the difference between the two cards.

Fred
